subject: design-technology
title: Foundations: Meet the 6 Rs
welcome_lead: Sort your bins and learn the 6 Rs that guide every sustainable design decision.
meta_desc: Learn the 6 Rs and core sustainability ideas for GCSE Design & Technology.
final_note: You can list the 6 Rs and apply each one to a product example.

concepts.def: Use less material and energy in the first place.
Use a product again for the same or new purpose.
Decline products that harm the environment.
Reimagine the way a product solves a need.
Fix broken products to extend life.

walkthroughs.body_html: The 6 Rs are ordered roughly best to last resort: Refuse, Rethink, Reduce, Reuse, Repair, Recycle. Recycling is often listed last because it still consumes energy. Refusing single-use plastic saves the most.
Refuse a plastic straw. Reduce by buying concentrated detergent. Reuse a glass jar as a pen pot. Repair jeans rather than buying new. Recycle aluminium cans into new cans.

A new phone applies Reduce (smaller charger box), Rethink (modular parts), Repair (replaceable battery) and Recycle (take-back scheme for metals). Designers earn marks by linking decisions to specific Rs.
